name: Stratum Executive Formal Dress Uniform
description:
Stratum's formal dress uniform is issued to management-tier employees for client presentations, regulatory appearances, and internal advancement ceremonies. The jacket is structured worsted synth-wool in deep charcoal with a subtle herringbone weave visible only in direct light. Rank insignia is embedded in the left breast in Stratum's standard chromatic thread — color-shifting from silver to gold depending on seniority level, verified by a micro-NFC chip that can be scanned at security checkpoints. The trousers are cut with a full-break hem and include a hidden cable-management channel along the left inner seam for BCI tether routing.

The uniform is not sold — it is issued, registered to the employee's ID, and must be returned upon separation from the company. Employees who leave Stratum under good terms receive a certificate allowing them to purchase the uniform at cost (Φ140). Employees separated for cause have the uniform remotely flagged — the chromatic thread shifts to a flat gray that doesn't respond to light, which is not subtle.
cultural_context: The Stratum dress uniform is recognized throughout Meridian's corporate corridors. Wearing one outside of Stratum employment is technically a terms-of-service violation but not illegal. Gray-market units with the NFC chips removed circulate among people who want the credibility signal without the affiliation. Stratum's security division runs periodic sweeps for flagged or unregistered units.
story_hooks: The character has a Stratum dress uniform with the NFC chip removed — bought gray-market. It gets them past three checkpoints before someone runs a visual ID cross-check and the story gets complicated.

The chromatic thread on a character's legitimately-issued uniform starts shifting to gray before they've received any separation notice. Either the system made an error, or someone inside Stratum has already decided their employment is ending.
A Stratum executive at a formal event is wearing a uniform with gold-level insignia, but the character's BCI flagged an NFC anomaly on the scan. The insignia might be fabricated.

physical_description.visual_profile: A sharp, authoritative silhouette that reads immediately as corporate management. The jacket sits structured and composed, broadcasting institutional legitimacy and middle-tier power. The trousers hang with military precision. The overall effect is controlled, vetted, legible to any security checkpoint in the GLMZ.
physical_description.fit: Tailored and precise — the jacket is cut with a contemporary business fit, slightly tapered at the waist without being fashion-forward. Trousers drape with a full break at the shoe, emphasizing formality over mobility. Sleeves end cleanly at the wrist. Nothing loose, nothing loud.
physical_description.primary_material: Worsted synth-wool — a high-grade biocomposite that mimics natural wool fiber structure but resists staining and climate shifts. Durable, professional, and entirely vegan.
physical_description.texture: Smooth and dense to the eye, with a subtle herringbone weave that catches light only at certain angles — a detail that signals quality control and attention to regulation aesthetics. Feels firm against the skin, structured to hold its shape through 12-hour shifts.
physical_description.color_scheme: Deep charcoal with near-black shadows. The herringbone pattern is so subtle it reads as solid until inspected. The rank insignia on the left breast is the only color detail — chromatic thread that shifts from cool silver (junior management) to warm gold (senior tiers) depending on the wearer's verified seniority level within Stratum's hierarchy.
physical_description.closures: Two-button jacket front with hidden magnetic snaps under the placket for rapid closure without audible clicking. Trousers fastened with a friction-fit waistband — no buckles or magnetic hardware to interfere with BCI tether routing. Clean, silent, corporate.
distinctive_features: Embedded micro-NFC rank insignia on left breast — color-shifting chromatic thread verified by security scanners
Hidden cable-management channel along left inner seam of trousers for BCI tether routing
Herringbone weave visible only under direct light — a subtle quality marker
Registration number embroidered inside right jacket pocket in UV-reactive thread (invisible under normal light)
Magnetic snap placket for silent closure
Full-break hem on trousers signaling formal context
Flat weave at collar and cuffs to reduce interference with augmentation hardware
physical_description.tier_indicator: Tier 3-4 issued corporate formal wear — aspirational for Tier 4 street-side workers, completely out of reach for Tier 5. The presence of this uniform in a room signals management access, regulated employment, and institutional trust.
physical_description.cultural_context: This is the uniform of stability within the GLMZ's corporate hierarchy. Wearing one means you passed background checks, you're synchronized with corpo schedules, and you have skin in the institution. Gray-market units with removed NFC chips circulate in street-level fashion — worn for the credibility signal alone, a calculated risk of legal friction. Stratum's security division occasionally flags separated-for-cause units, turning the chromatic rank insignia an inert gray that refuses to shift — a walking shame marker.
physical_description.condition_typical: Pristine to well-broken-in depending on tenure. New issue is crisp and responsive. After months of wear, it develops a soft drape and refined patina that reads as seniority. Units owned after separation tend toward immaculate preservation — they're investments, not daily wear. Gray-market units are often carefully aged to look legitimate.
